instructions: Tools for a real Godot 4 editor running on a GPU in a container. The person may be watching it live in the Godot panel beside the chat, and one editor is shared by every chat and the person, so check list_projects before you replace what is open. Every editor edit you make (add_node, set_property, attach_script, write_file, ...) happens in that editor and goes through its undo history. Typical loop: list_projects / new_project / open_project -> open_scene or new_scene -> add_node / set_property / attach_script -> save_scene -> check_scripts -> run_project -> screenshot(target=game) and get_output -> stop -> record or export. File paths are res:// paths inside the open project; nothing outside it can be read or written. Property values are JSON: [x, y] for Vector2, "#rrggbb" for Color, "res://..." to load a resource, {"type": "RectangleShape2D", "size": [32, 32]} for a new resource, {"$expr": "..."} for any Godot expression. execute_gdscript runs arbitrary GDScript in the editor for anything the other tools do not cover. If the editor stops answering, restart_editor restarts it.

tools.name: ping
tools.description: Versions (Godot, server), the GPU the container renders on, the open project and its renderer, and the editor's own report (graphics adapter, rendering method, open scenes, whether a game is running).

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: Projects on the server (data/projects/<name>), most recently changed first, with each one's renderer and whether it has a web export. `open` names the project the editor has open.

tools.name: new_project
tools.description: Create a project from a template and (by default) open it in the editor. 2d: a Node2D main scene, Compatibility renderer (what web exports use; lightest on the GPU). 3d: a Node3D main scene with a camera, sun and sky, Forward+ renderer. Both have Web and Linux export presets.

name.description: Folder and project name (letters, digits, space, _ - .)

tools.name: open_project
tools.description: Open another project. The editor saves its open scenes, restarts on the new project (a few seconds; longer the first time while it imports) and the stream follows.

tools.name: restart_editor
tools.description: Restart the editor on the open project. Use it when the editor stops answering (an endless execute_gdscript or @tool script, a stuck dialog). If it still answers it saves its open scenes and quits first; if not it is killed and unsaved changes are lost. previous_editor says which.

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: Files and folders in the open project (the .godot cache, .import and .uid files are left out unless include_meta).

path.description: A res:// path inside the open project (a path relative to the project root also works).

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a file of the open project: text as content, anything else as content_base64.

path.description: A res:// path inside the open project (a path relative to the project root also works).

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Create or overwrite a file in the open project. The editor writes it, so it notices at once: a script open in the script editor shows the new text, an open scene reloads. Use attach_script to put a script on a node.

path.description: A res:// path inside the open project (a path relative to the project root also works).

tools.name: delete_file
tools.description: Delete a file of the open project (with its .import / .uid companions). A scene that is open in the editor has its tab closed first (dropping unsaved changes in it), so no later save writes it back.

path.description: A res:// path inside the open project (a path relative to the project root also works).

tools.name: get_scene_tree
tools.description: The scene open in the editor as a tree: name, type, path (relative to the root, which is what node arguments take), script, and a few key values (position, size, text, texture, shape).

tools.name: open_scene
tools.description: Open a scene (.tscn or .scn) in the editor (it becomes the edited scene; other open scenes stay in their tabs).

path.description: A res:// path inside the open project (a path relative to the project root also works).

tools.name: new_scene
tools.description: Create a scene file with one root node, save it and open it. set_main makes it the project's main scene (what run_project and exports start).

root_type.description: Node class or a class_name script

root_name.description: Default: the file name in PascalCase

tools.name: add_node
tools.description: Add a node to the edited scene, through the editor's undo history, and select it so it shows in the Scene dock and Inspector. Give type for a new node or scene to instance a .tscn. Values are JSON: [x, y] for a Vector2, [x, y, z] for a Vector3, "#rrggbb" or [r, g, b, a] (0-1) for a Color, "res://..." to load a resource, a class name or {"type": "CircleShape2D", "radius": 20} for a new resource, {"$expr": "Vector2(1, 2) * 3"} for any Godot expression.

type.description: Node class (Sprite2D, CharacterBody2D, Label, ...) or a class_name script

scene.description: A .tscn to instance instead of type. A res:// path inside the open project (a path relative to the project root also works).

parent.description: Path from the scene root ("." is the root)

properties.description: Property name -> value, set before the node is added

tools.name: set_property
tools.description: Set one or more properties of a node in the edited scene (one undoable action). Sub-properties work with a colon: position:x. Values are JSON: [x, y] for a Vector2, [x, y, z] for a Vector3, "#rrggbb" or [r, g, b, a] (0-1) for a Color, "res://..." to load a resource, a class name or {"type": "CircleShape2D", "radius": 20} for a new resource, {"$expr": "Vector2(1, 2) * 3"} for any Godot expression.

tools.name: delete_node
tools.description: Delete a node (and its children) from the edited scene; undoable.

tools.name: attach_script
tools.description: Attach a GDScript to a node (undoable), writing it first when source is given, and open it in the script editor. Returns compiles (Godot's --check-only) and the errors if not.

source.description: GDScript source to write to path first

tools.name: save_scene
tools.description: Save the edited scene (to path when given: Save As, a .tscn or .scn path), or every open scene with all.

path.description: A res:// path inside the open project (a path relative to the project root also works).

tools.name: reload
tools.description: Make the editor pick up files changed outside it: rescan the project (and reload changed open scripts), or reload just the given paths. write_file does this by itself.

tools.name: run_project
tools.description: Run the project's main scene from the editor, the way the Play button does. The game opens in a window over the editor, visible in the stream. Returns output_mark for get_output, and the errors printed so far. A game that stops in the editor's debugger (a script parse or runtime error) returns playing false and halted with the error and its file:line.

tools.name: run_scene
tools.description: Run the edited scene, or the scene at path, from the editor.

path.description: A res:// path inside the open project (a path relative to the project root also works).

tools.name: stop
tools.description: Stop the game the editor is running.

tools.name: get_output
tools.description: The editor's output: its own messages and those of the game it runs (print(), errors, warnings, script errors with their line), newest last. Pass since (a mark from run_project or an earlier get_output) to get only what came after it. While the game is stopped in the editor's debugger, playing is false and halted gives the error and its file:line.

tools.name: check_scripts
tools.description: Parse and type-check GDScript files (all of the project's, outside addons/, or the given paths) with Godot's --check-only, and return each failing file's errors with line numbers.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: An image of the editor (target editor: the whole window; 2d / 3d: that viewport), the running game's window (game), or the whole streamed screen (screen).

max_width.description: Scale editor images down to this width

tools.name: record
tools.description: Record the game with Movie Maker on the GPU: a fixed frame rate, so the result is smooth however long each frame takes. Saves data/renders/<project>/<time>/movie.mp4 (or the PNG frames) and returns a frame from the middle.

tools.name: export
tools.description: Export the open project (open scenes are saved first). web: a single-threaded HTML5 build under data/exports/<project>/web. linux: an x86_64 binary and .pck under data/exports/<project>/linux. The person downloads either as a .zip from the Godot panel's project menu; to show the game running, use run_project.

tools.name: execute_gdscript
tools.description: ARBITRARY CODE: run GDScript inside the editor process (as an EditorScript would) and return what it prints and returns. The code is the body of a function run(); these are in scope: scene_root (the edited scene's root), undo_redo (EditorUndoRedoManager), plugin (EditorPlugin), and EditorInterface. Changes made here bypass the undo history unless you use undo_redo. Prefer the specific tools; use this for anything they do not cover (project settings, input map, signals, bulk edits). The editor does nothing else while the code runs: an endless loop freezes it until restart_editor.

code.description: GDScript statements (or a full script defining func run())
